articles.title: Report Card Grades for Top 20 College Football QBs after Week 4
articles.summary: Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.
articles.body:
Every Tuesday morning throughout the 2026 college football season, we will be grading the performance of the top 20 quarterbacks in the nation, then re-ranking a new top 20 for next week's report card assignment.

Included are each player's numbers through the air and on the ground, their game's outcome, and the quality of their opponent. A 1-5 star system was used to highlight the quality of the opponent, using the most recent version of The Athletic 's ranking of all 138 FBS teams, with stars awarded as follows:

5 stars: No. 1-10 in the rankings 4 stars: No. 11-40 in the rankings 3 stars: No. 41-70 in the rankings 2 stars: No. 71-100 in the rankings 1 star: No. 101-138 in the rankings or an FCS opponent

Each quarterback's performance was given a grade of A, B, C, D or F. Those grades were factored into the reordering of the rankings for the following week.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 30-of-50, 292 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, 38 yards Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Cincinnati) Week 4 Outcome: Loss (26-31)

Avery Johnson racked up 227 passing yards and 152 rushing yards in a 31-20 victory over Tulane in Week 3 to climb into the rankings, but he was mostly kept in check in a loss to Cincinnati.

With 58 total touchdowns over 25 games in the 2024 and 2025 seasons, Johnson has been a dynamic dual-threat option throughout his time at Kansas State. Saturday marked the first time this season that he did not account for multiple scores.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 15-of-27, 212 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 10 carries, 66 yards Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Michigan State) Week 4 Outcome: Win (31-13)

Nebraska is 4-0 for the first time since 2016, when Tommy Armstrong Jr. led them to a 9-4 season and a trip to the Music City Bowl. Anthony Colandrea has been one of the nation's more productive transfer quarterbacks early on.

He has completed 65.4 percent of his passes, right in line with his 65.9 percent completion rate at UNLV in 2025. Saturday was his first real test against a quality opponent. He has now tallied 904 passing yards, 141 rushing yards and 12 total touchdowns on the year.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 21-of-27, 365 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 8 carries, 35 yards, 1 TD Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (South Carolina) Week 4 Outcome: Win (49-18)

Things have clicked for Keelon Russell over the past two weeks after a slow start to the season, as the former 5-star recruit is looking the part in his first year under center for the Crimson Tide:

Week 1-2: 34-of-53, 444 yards, 1 TD, 2 INT; 21 carries, 77 yards, 1 TD Week 3-4: 44-of-57, 685 yards, 7 TD, 0 INT; 11 carries, 91 yards, 2 TD

Now, a grueling stretch of the calendar begins as they face Mississippi State, Georgia, Tennessee and Texas A&M over a span of four weeks. That will put his breakthrough performance to the test.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 22-of-35, 147 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, -3 yards Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Boston College) Week 4 Outcome: Win (21-14)

Ethan Grunkemeyer leads the ACC with 101 completions through four games. After connecting on 69.1 percent of his attempts at Penn State a year ago, he has upped that to 74.3 percent this season while piloting the Hokies to a 4-0 start.

His 7.4 yards per attempt keeps him out of the nation's elite tier of signal callers for the time being. Virginia Tech has leaned heavily on the running game with 177.8 rushing yards per game. Still, the stability he has provided under center has already helped the team surpass last year's win total.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 22-of-36, 297 yards, 4 TD, 1 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 11 carries, 20 yards Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Washington State) Week 4 Outcome: Win (34-24)

With 622 yards and eight touchdowns through the air in the last two weeks against Northern Illinois and Washington State, Noah Fifita now leads the Big 12 in completions (99), completion percentage (75.6) and passing touchdowns (11).

If he can lead Arizona to victories over Cincinnati and West Virginia over the next two weeks, they could roll into their bye week with a spot in the AP Top 25 poll. His efficiency and high-level production could continue to push him up the rankings.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 10-of-22, 132 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 28 carries, 103 yards, 3 TD Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Oklahoma State) Week 4 Outcome: Loss (24-41)

Michael Hawkins Jr. ranks 10th in the nation and leads all quarterbacks with 425 rushing yards. He has found the end zone nine times on the ground while logging 5.9 yards per carry.

His passing production has essentially been icing on the cake, though the West Virginia offense hit a wall down the stretch on Saturday with three turnovers on downs and a punt over their final four possessions as a 24-21 lead flipped to a 41-24 loss.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 8-of-10, 77 yards, 0 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 1 carry, 10 yards Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (USC) Week 4 Outcome: Win (41-27)

Dante Moore left the field on an ambulance during the second quarter of Saturday's game after USC linebacker Desman Stephens delivered an illegal hit that led to his ejection.

"He's in recovery, so I don't want to speak too soon, but he is moving, and he does have the ability to move," head coach Dan Lanning told reporters .

Backup Dylan Raiola completed 19-of-25 pass attempts for 289 yards and two touchdowns in relief to help lead Oregon to victory, a week after connecting on all 11 of his passes for 124 yards and three scores.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 17-of-22, 239 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, 14 yards, 2 TD Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Georgia Southern) Week 4 Outcome: Win (42-28)

A shaky day from the Houston defense and a successful onside kick made things interesting in a game where the Cougars were 18.5-point favorites, but Conner Weigman led the offense on six straight touchdown drives to help avoid the upset and seize control of what was a 14-14 game.

His 14 total touchdowns trail only Kamario Taylor (16), Jayden Maiava (16) and Darian Mensah (15). He has completed 71.6 percent of his passes, up from 65.2 percent during his breakout 2025 campaign.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 12-of-29, 114 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 10 carries, 23 yards, 1 TD Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Wisconsin) Week 4 Outcome: Loss (20-24)

After completing 70.3 percent of his throws for 751 yards and nine touchdowns in wins over Marshall, Temple and Buffalo, Rocco Becht turned in a dud in his first game against a major conference opponent.

The Nittany Lions managed just 233 yards of total offense, including 3.9 yards per pass attempt. They failed to put any points on the board in their final five offensive possessions. They will look to rebound on the road against Northwestern on Friday.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 14-of-22, 237 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 3 carries, 10 yards, 1 TD Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★ (Purdue) Week 4 Outcome: Win (49-10)

After a quiet Week 3 performance against Michigan State, where he finished without a passing touchdown, CJ Carr led the onslaught in a lopsided victory on the road against Purdue on Saturday with four total touchdowns.

He quietly passed Joe Theismann to move into 10th all-time in Notre Dame history with 33 career passing touchdowns. His 172.2 passer rating sits atop the leaderboard among quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 27-of-36, 367 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 29 yards, 1 TD Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Illinois) Week 4 Outcome: Win (42-19)

The Julian Sayin-to-Jeremiah Smith connection reached new heights against the Illinois defense, as the All-American wide receiver hauled in 12 catches for 217 yards and four touchdowns.

There is little doubt that having such a dominant No. 1 target is benefiting Sayin, but he still has to get him the football. He is putting together another extremely efficient season, leading the Big Ten with a 72.2 percent completion rate while averaging 301.5 passing yards per game.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 18-of-27, 206 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 21 yards Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Iowa State) Week 4 Outcome: Win (31-17)

Devon Dampier has yet to eclipse 50 rushing yards in a game this season, but Utah has not needed him to win games with his legs. Keeping him healthy after a banged-up 2025 season is the No. 1 priority.

His completion percentage has increased from 57.9 to 63.5 to 70.3 percent in his three years as a starter. He now ranks among the most efficient passers in the nation. The Utes are up to No. 13 in the latest AP poll, just one spot behind Big 12 favorite Texas Tech.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 27-of-36, 324 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

Week 4 Rushing Stats: 13 carries, -19 yards, 2 TD

Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Wake Forest)

Saturday's loss dropped Louisville to 2-2 on the year and knocked the team out of the AP poll, but Lincoln Kienholz remains one of college football's biggest breakout stars after transferring from Ohio State during the offseason.

He drove Louisville into field-goal range twice in the fourth quarter with a chance to tie the game, but the first attempt was missed and the second was blocked.

Still, the ACC remains wide open, and the Cardinals' win over SMU could loom large if they rebound from this disappointing start.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 14-of-19, 201 yards, 0 TD, 1 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 11 carries, -1 yard Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Tennessee) Week 4 Outcome: Win (20-17)

The Longhorns pulled off a big road win against Tennessee on two rushing touchdowns by Raleek Brown and a 10-sack performance by the defense, while Arch Manning had limited impact on the outcome.

"It's not about me," Manning said in his postgame interview . "I didn't play very well, but our team played great. Defense played well."

Since throwing four touchdown passes in the opener against Texas State, Manning has completed 60.2 percent of his throws for 557 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions in his last three games.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 27-of-38, 360 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 10 carries, 7 yards Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Missouri) Week 4 Outcome: Win (31-24)

In his first career start against a ranked opponent, Kamario Taylor continued his breakout season, recording a fourth straight game with at least three touchdown passes. He leads the SEC in passing touchdowns (14) and ties Jayden Maiava for the FBS lead in total touchdowns (16). Maiava has played one more game.

If they can pull off the upset at home against Alabama next weekend, it would be the first time the Bulldogs have started the season 5-0 since 2014, when Dak Prescott led them to a 10-3 finish.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 19-of-29, 201 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, 1 yard, 1 TD Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Northwestern) Week 4 Outcome: Win (29-23)

After back-to-back shutouts, the Indiana defense struggled on Friday night against Northwestern, while quarterback Josh Hoover averaged a season-low 6.9 yards per attempt and found the end zone once with his arm and once with his legs.

The Hoosiers were ultimately bailed out by running back Lee Bebee Jr. (24 carries, 203 yards, 1 TD), avoiding the upset in a game where they were 20.5-point favorites. Hoover has been efficient, but he is still searching for his first 300-yard passing performance in an Indiana uniform. He should have a chance to put up some numbers on the road against Rutgers next Saturday.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 14-of-25, 171 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 5 carries, 0 yards Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★ (Oklahoma) Week 4 Outcome: Win (41-13)

The Bulldogs had three rushing touchdowns, two field goals and a defensive score in their lopsided win over Oklahoma, so most of the damage on the scoreboard on Saturday came outside of the passing game.

Georgia has outscored the opposition by a 219-53 margin so far this year. However, after throwing eight total touchdown passes against Tennessee State and Western Kentucky, Gunner Stockton has been held below 200 passing yards in back-to-back games, with two touchdowns and one interception.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 23-of-42, 326 yards, 2 TD, 1 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 6 carries, 1 yard, 1 TD Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Oregon) Week 4 Outcome: Loss (27-41)

Jayden Maiava led a seven-play, 75-yard drive to tie the game at 27-27 with 12:41 remaining in the fourth quarter, but Oregon responded with back-to-back touchdown drives, while USC settled for a turnover on downs and an interception to close out a disappointing loss.

Maiava leads the FBS in passing yards (1,499). While he has played one more game than most quarterbacks, his 299.8 yards per game is a slight improvement over last year's 285.5 mark, when he led the Big Ten in passing.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 25-of-34, 298 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

Week 4 Rushing Stats: 7 carries, 44 yards, 2 TD

Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★★★★ (Florida)

Ole Miss allowed 302 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the ground in a blowout loss to Florida, crashing back to earth one week after its top-10 victory over LSU.

Trinidad Chambliss did what he could to keep Ole Miss competitive. His interception came on the final drive, when the outcome was already decided. Despite the final scoreboard, he continues to have a Heisman-caliber season, leading the SEC in completions (102) and passing yards (1,222) while tallying 12 total touchdowns.

Week 4 Passing Stats: 23-of-27, 338 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT Week 4 Rushing Stats: 4 carries, 21 yards, 1 TD Week 4 Quality of Opponent: ★ (Central Michigan) Week 4 Outcome: Win (52-3)

It's rare for a quarterback to complete 23 of 27 passes in his fourth game of the season and still see his season completion percentage drop, but that's how efficient Darian Mensah has been this year.

He remains the FBS leader in completion percentage (88.7) and passer rating (228.2). He added his first rushing touchdown of the season on Saturday, joining his 14 passing scores. A road game against Clemson next week will provide his first true high-profile test of the season.

To keep things fresh and include breakout performers, we will re-rank the top 20 quarterbacks each week on this final slide. That will then reset the field for next week's report cards.

articles.title: B/R's 2026 Heisman Trophy Odds and Rankings after Week 4
articles.summary: As the opening month of the college football season comes to a close, the tone of the 2026 Heisman Trophy conversation is also shifting.
articles.body:
As the opening month of the college football season comes to a close, the tone of the 2026 Heisman Trophy conversation is also shifting.

Early on, preseason expectations linger. It's generally wise not to overreact to what happens during nonconference action, especially given the potential for dramatic differences in competition level.

However, when league play begins, the results become more significant.

After a weekend in which eight AP Top 25 teams lost, a deluge of updates to the Heisman race is only reasonable.

While the latest FanDuel odds are listed, the rankings are more subjective as a snapshot of this moment in the season.

Kamario Taylor, QB, Mississippi State (+800)

Trinidad Chambliss, QB, Ole Miss (+1100)

Nate Sheppard, RB, Duke : The nation's leading rusher, Sheppard has surpassed the 100-yard mark in all four victories so far. He's picked up 644 yards and six scores on the ground, while also catching 10 passes for three more touchdowns. Duke has an open weekend before heading to Georgia Tech.

Josh Hoover, QB, Indiana : Although it was closer than anticipated, Indiana beat Northwestern to hit 4-0. Hoover threw for 202 yards and two scores, lifting his season production to 871 yards with 12 touchdowns and no turnovers. Indiana plays at Rutgers in Week 5.

Drew Mestemaker, QB, Oklahoma State : Since the ugly season-opening loss at Tulsa, Mestemaker has propelled Oklahoma State to three straight wins. He just threw for 389 yards and three scores in a victory at West Virginia. UCF awaits in Week 6.

Arch Manning, QB, Texas : The good news is that Manning has helped Texas to a 4-0 record, including a vital win over Ohio State. His numbers, however, have been merely solid. After an open date, the Longhorns will face rival Oklahoma and then five consecutive opponents currently ranked in the Top 25. Manning has a lot to prove.

Devon Dampier, QB, Utah : Dampier has propelled Utah to four consecutive wins and a No. 13 ranking in the AP poll. So far, he's passed for 896 yards and scampered for 135 yards with 11 total touchdowns to one interception. Utah has an extra week to prepare for Kansas.

Keelon Russell, QB, Alabama : Russell's surge continued in a smackdown of South Carolina. While guiding the Tide to a 49-18 win, he racked up exactly 400 yards and totaled five touchdowns. Russell is entering a very challenging three-week window at Mississippi State, home to Georgia and at Tennessee.

Gunner Stockton, QB, Georgia : Stockton tossed his first interception of the year last weekend. Bummer. Anyway, he threw for 171 yards and a score in a 41-13 demolition of Oklahoma. Stockton has accounted for 854 yards and 10 scores as UGA enters a Week 5 clash with Vanderbilt.

Malachi Toney, WR, Miami : Were it not for a questionable penalty, Toney would've had a second score—and an absurd highlight—to bolster his résumé. Instead, he settled for six catches, 120 yards and a touchdown in Miami's 52-3 rout of Central Michigan. Next for Toney and the 'Canes is a key ACC matchup at Clemson on Saturday in prime time.

CJ Carr, QB, Notre Dame : Notre Dame's blowout streak continued as it defeated all four September opponents by 17-plus points. Carr threw for 237 yards and three scores, with an interception, in a 49-10 win over Purdue, then added a fourth touchdown on the ground. ND plays at North Carolina this weekend.

Julian Sayin, QB, Ohio State : Despite taking a back seat to teammate Jeremiah Smith, Sayin has been extremely productive. He's thrown for 1,206 yards at 10.6 per attempt—both ranking eighth nationally—with 12 total scores and a lone interception. Ohio State, though, may need an efficient showing from Sayin to navigate a tricky Week 5 game at Iowa.

Perceptions change quickly in college football.

Last week, Trinidad Chambliss found himself the target of praise, adoration and a whole lot of other kind words. Fast-forward seven days, and that dramatic win over LSU has taken a back seat to a lopsided loss at Florida.

Chambliss still passed for 298 yards, rushed for 44 and threw for three touchdowns. He kept the Rebels competitive until UF owned the fourth quarter.

Ole Miss's main problem is a defense prone to giving up explosive plays. In turn, it shifts a mountain of pressure onto Chambliss and the offense to survive in high-scoring games.

If there's a bright side, it means Chambliss should have impressive box scores.

If the Rebels continue to flail defensively, it'll be tough to avoid more losses—and push Chambliss in the wrong direction for the Heisman.

The challenge with an early top performer like Jadan Baugh is projecting what's ahead. Sure, he flat-out dominated Florida Atlantic, Campbell and Auburn, but how seriously did we need to take a revamped UF team?

Florida obliterated fourth-ranked Ole Miss behind a powerful offense that included Baugh, racing to 142 yards and three touchdowns. He added a 12-yard reception in the air during the Gators' head-turning 52-28 win.

Through four weeks, the junior ranks second nationally with 600 rushing yards and leads the country with 11 scores on the ground.

While the UF schedule doesn't get much easier—a trip to No. 25 Missouri awaits this weekend—Baugh and the Gators are now squarely in the national eye.

3. Kamario Taylor, QB, Mississippi State

The hype is about to take a serious test.

The nation's breakout player of September, Kamario Taylor, ended the month on a high note. He oversaw a fourth-quarter comeback to beat Missouri, throwing for 360 yards and three touchdowns in a dramatic 31-24 win.

Mississippi State is 4-0 for the second time since 2014, when the program held the AP No. 1 ranking for a full month.

That pesky powerhouse looms for MSU, which at least has the advantage of hosting Saturday's game. Even as the underdog, the Taylor-led upstart has a huge opportunity ahead in the early afternoon showdown.

Last week, I mentioned that other candidates have flashier stats and Smith would benefit from a big afternoon in Week 4.

He obviously saw this ranking and took it to heart.

During a 42-19 thrashing of Illinois, Smith pulled in 12 passes for 217 yards and four touchdowns. Most impressively, he set a career-high mark in each category while helping the Buckeyes move to 3-1.

The main priority for Smith and OSU is winning at Iowa on Saturday. That's the measure of success, no doubt.

Nevertheless, the junior receiver only needs 10 receptions and two scores to become the program's all-time leader in both categories. Smith already took the yardage mark two weeks ago.

When a quarterback matches a season-worst total of four incompletions in the fourth game of the season, you know things are going well.

Darian Mensah hit 23-of-27 attempts in a 52-3 rout of Central Michigan, ending the opening month with a 94-of-106 line. That would be an 88.7 completion rate, which is just absurd at this level.

Overall, he's thrown for 1,211 yards and still has more touchdowns (14) than errant passes (12), with zero turnovers. Mensah slithered past two CMU defenders for a first rushing score of the year as well.

The numbers likely won't be near-perfect much longer, of course.

Miami travels to Clemson this weekend, and four unbeaten teams—Pitt, Notre Dame, Duke and Virginia Tech—remain on the slate. It's pretty unconscionable to believe he can sustain this hot of a start.

But there's not much reason to believe Mensah won't still be excellent, either.

articles.title: Cambios en la cúpula del Barça
articles.standfirst: Manel Del Río, director general desde hace justo un año, deja la entidad
articles.summary: Manel Del Río, director general desde hace justo un año, deja la entidad
articles.body: La Dirección del Barcelona sufre una importante baja: Manel Del Río, director general del club catalán desde hace un año, abandona la entidad azulgrana. Sergio Serrano asumirá, de momento, parte de sus funciones al frente del área financiera. Del Río comunicó, hace ya bastantes días, al presidente Joan Laporta su decisión de dejar a finales de este mes de septiembre, el Barcelona, pero fue este lunes cuando se despidió del Comité de Dirección. Ayer, según adelantó el Diari Ara y confirmó MARCA, se oficializó su baja, que, según comentan fuentes del Barça, ha sido de mutuo acuerdo, aunque no especifican ni concretan los motivos. Manel Del Río llegó al club azulgrana en 2022, asumiendo el cargo de director financiero y corporativo, y hace justo un año, en septiembre de 2025, fue nombrado director general de la entidad, puesto que estaba vacía desde que Ferran Reverter renunciara en 2022. De momento, la plaza de director general del Barça quedará vacante a la espera de encontrarle un sustituto a Del Río, aunque Sergio Serrano, profesional que procede del Banco Sabadell, asumirá buena parte de sus funciones: liderará la dirección financiera del Barcelona. Serrano llegó a la entidad el pasado mes de junio y fue, por ejemplo, el encargado de exponer y explicar en la pasada Asamblea Ordinaria de Compromisarios los números del cierre del último ejercicio económico del Barça y el presupuesto de la presente campaña.

articles.title: El Barça, en alerta: Raphinha, sustituido con Brasil por molestias musculares en la pierna derecha
articles.standfirst: El azulgrana no pudo continuar el partido amistoso contra Australia
articles.summary: El azulgrana no pudo continuar el partido amistoso contra Australia
articles.body: Malas noticias para el Barcelona. La CBF informó que Raphinha tuvo que ser sustituido en el descanso del partido amistoso de este martes entre Brasil y Australia por unas molestias musculares en el muslo derecho. Los peores temores del Barça se confirmaron. El atacante del Barcelona disputó toda la primera parte con aparente normalidad, pero Raphinha fue sustituido en el descanso. Según informó la Federación brasileña, tras la reanudación, el cambio se debió a unas molestias musculares en la pierna derecha. El exprofesional del Leeds salió de titular en el cruce contra Australia, y Ancelotti había apostado por él como falso 9. Había marcado incluso un gol, de penalti. Fue el 2-2, el tanto del empate. Pero en el descanso, Raphinha, que lucía el 10 y el brazalete de capitán, fue sustituido por las molestias. Entró Endrick en su lugar. El jugador, de acuerdo con el preparador, decidió parar y no correr más riesgos. Es una zona, además, en la que el futbolista internacional ya ha tenido algunos problemas recientemente, de ahí, la máxima precaución. De hecho, regresó de anteriores citaciones con Brasil lesionado del muslo. Debido a esta dolencia, el curso pasado, el 25-26, no tuvo la continuidad deseada y se perdió 26 encuentros, entre el Barcelona y su combinado nacional. Es su punto débil. Raphinha será examinado en las próximas horas para evaluar el alcance exacto de su dolencia, una vez concluya el compromiso que se disputa en el estadio Suncorp Stadium. Brasil todavía tiene un partido más por disputar: el que jugará en la India el próximo sábado. En función de los resultados de las pruebas, el culé seguirá con su selección o adelantará su vuelta. En la rueda de prensa posterior al compromiso en Australia, Carlo Ancelotti no fue cuestionado por la salida forzosa del atacante del terreno de juego. Brasil se impuso al final por 2-4. En el Barcelona cruzan los dedos y confían en que la dolencia no sea grave. Raphinha es su jugador más determinante en estos momentos: ha marcado 14 goles. El club culé, que ya vio hace unos días cómo Éric García tenía que regresar de su citación con España por molestias en la rodilla, ve ahora cómo el brasileño, que ya retornó lesionado de su participación con su combinado nacional en anteriores citas, también paga la acumulación de minutos.

articles.title: La lesión de Alberto Díaz crea un problema de base a la selección
articles.standfirst: El capitán del Unicaja estará dos meses parado y seguramente se pierda la Ventana FIBA de noviembre, cuando Chus Mateo no podrá llamar a jugadores de NBA ni de Euroliga
articles.summary: El capitán del Unicaja estará dos meses parado y seguramente se pierda la Ventana FIBA de noviembre, cuando Chus Mateo no podrá llamar a jugadores de NBA ni de Euroliga
articles.body: Alberto Díaz tendrá que estar cerca de dos meses de baja debido a la rotura fibrilar que sufrió en el isquiotibial de la pierna izquierda durante el partido disputado este domingo en el Movistar Arena frente al Real Madrid. La lesión del capitán del Unicaja, uno de los fijos de la selección en las Ventanas FIBA, crea un problema de base para Chus Mateo. España se va a jugar a finales de noviembre buena parte de sus aspiraciones de clasificación para la Copa del Mundo. El día 26 de ese mes la selección visitará a Montenegro y el 29 recibirá a Grecia en el Fontes do Sar de Santiago de Compostela. A esas dos citas, salvo que acorte sus plazos de recuperación, no podrá llegar Alberto Díaz. Y sin posibilidad de contar con jugadores de NBA y Euroliga, el asunto se complica. Mateo no podrá contar con Sergio De Larrea, que ya habrá comenzado su primer curso con los Mavericks, ni con Álvaro Cárdenas y Mario Saint- Supéry, bases del Valencia Basket. Ellos tres y Díaz fueron los timones elegidos por el seleccionador en la última Ventana. Ahora no tendrá a ninguno de ellos y las opciones disminuyen considerablemente. Ferrán Bassas y Rafa Villar, del Manresa, y Guillem Vives y Sergi García, del Zaragoza, y la esperanza del regreso de Ricky Rubio aparecen como opciones. Tampoco sería descartable que se recurriera a Carlos Alocén (Granca) o Lluis Costa (Granada) pese a estar jugando en clubes de la Primera FEB. Después de tres derrotas consecutivas -Georgia, Portugal y Grecia- la selección se ha complicado el billete para el Mundial de Qatar del próximo verano. La clasificación se ha apretado con Ucrania en primer puesto con un balance de 6-2. España está igualada con Georgia en la segunda plaza con 5-3. Lo bueno es que a ambas les tiene ganado el average. Lo malo es que por detrás, con 4-4, vienen ya Portugal, Grecia y Montenegro. De ahí que los siguientes dos encuentros sean trascendentales. Tras la Ventana de noviembre todavía quedará otra a finales de febrero y comienzos de marzo. Ahí, España visitará a Portugal y recibirá a Montenegro. Del grupo de seis selecciones, sólo las tres primeras conseguirán la clasificación para el Mundial.

articles.title: What did Yamal say to Messi at World Cup final? ‘Thank you for everything’
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal shared a warm embrace with Lionel Messi, thanking the Argentinian icon for everything he gave to football.
articles.body:
Two months after Spain dethroned Argentina as FIFA World Cup winners, Lamine Yamal has revealed what he said to a crestfallen Lionel Messi after the full-time whistle was blown in the final in the United States.

The teenage superstar thanked the football icon for “everything you gave football” as the pair shared a warm embrace on the pitch, Yamal said in an interview published in British media on Tuesday.

An extra-time goal by Ferran Torres in the July 19 final in East Rutherford, New Jersey, handed Spain their second World Cup crown as 2022 holders Argentina failed to win a title for the first time in three major tournaments.

In what was Yamal’s first World Cup final and Messi’s last, their hug was seen as a passing-of-the-torch moment between one of football’s greats and a player earmarked to build on his trophy-laden career in the future.

“I said thank you for everything you gave football,” Yamal told The Guardian newspaper.

“I don’t do things to look nice for the photo. That came from inside.”

Before the final, much of the attention had centred on the battle between 39-year-old Messi and 19-year-old Yamal, with the match likened to a master vs apprentice clash.

The hype reached fever pitch after social media was flooded with the viral photo of a young Messi bathing baby Yamal during a TV commercial. At first, many thought it was an AI-generated image, but it’s indeed real and dates back to 2007.

During a UNICEF fundraising shoot at his former club Barcelona’s Camp Nou stadium, a 20-year-old Messi met Yamal, who was only five months old at the time and accompanied by his mother, Sheila Ebana.

The photo was publicly shared by Yamal’s father two years ago, which begged the question: Why didn’t he post it earlier?

“Because I told him not to,” Yamal said. “He put it on Facebook once, and I told him to take it down.”

“Comparisons were too easy. That was all people would talk about. I wanted to be Lamine. I didn’t want to be Messi. I just wanted to get where I could get. I asked him to wait.”

“When I’m Lamine, do what you want,” he added.

Both Messi and Yamal are products of Barcelona’s famous La Masia academy, where the Spanish star joined at seven years of age but the Argentinian joined from his home country when he was 13.

While the 19-year-old has a long way to go before he matches Messi’s accolades, Yamal has already won the World Cup and the European Championship. Messi won his first and only World Cup in 2022 but has two Copa America titles to his name.

Both players have won multiple Spanish La Liga titles with Messi collecting 10 in his 17 years at Barcelona compared with Yamal’s three consecutive triumphs since making his senior team debut in 2023.

articles.title: Turkish referees' chief among seven arrested in corruption investigation
articles.summary:
The head of Turkey's referees' committee is detained along with six others as part of an investigation into corruption. 

head of Turkey’s referees committee, is among seven people detained in an investigation into alleged mobbing and document forgery
articles.body:
The head of the Turkish referees' body has been arrested as part of a police investigation into corruption.

Turkish justice minister Akin Gurlek said the investigation focused on "claims regarding interference in the formation of referee classifications, assignments, scoring and appointment processes, as well as rule examinations".

Ferhat Gundogdu, the president of the refereeing body, his vice-president and another five people are those arrested.

Gurlek said police also searched homes, workplaces and offices.

"We will resolutely continue our fight for clean football so that allegations damaging trust in Turkish football are brought to light, those responsible are held accountable before the law, and football is associated with the effort, competition and sportsmanship on the pitch," Gurlek said.

In November 2025 the Turkish Football Federation (TFF) suspended 149 referees and assistant referees after an investigation found hundreds of professional match officials in the country had betting accounts.

Some 29 people were arrested in the sprawling scandal, including 14 footballers.

However, Gurlek did not make any link between last year's betting scandal and the current investigation.

articles.title: Graham Alexander: New Preston North End boss says returning to club is 'surreal'
articles.summary: New Preston North End boss Graham Alexander says he feels like he has come home after returning to his old club as manager.
articles.body:
New Preston North End boss Graham Alexander has said he feels like he has come home.

The 54-year-old, who made 372 league appearances for the club across two spells as a player, left League One leaders Bradford City to succeed Paul Heckingbottom at Deepdale on Monday.

Alexander has taken over a North End side that are second from bottom in the Championship with six defeats from their opening eight league games.

"Yesterday was a bit surreal - it didn't feel real until I had the training kit on," he told BBC Radio Lancashire.

"When I got home last night, me and my wife had a bit of a moment about the journey we've had to get to this point."

Alexander retired as a player with Preston at the end of the 2011-12 season aged 40, having had a brief spell as caretaker at Deepdale during that campaign.

He turned down the option to start his coaching career in the club's academy and has subsequently managed Fleetwood, Scunthorpe, Salford City, Motherwell and MK Dons.

When asked if Preston felt like home, he said: "It does yeah, it does.

"When I took the Motherwell job it was a big decision from my wife and myself to move to Scotland because we'd been so happy in Preston for 20 years but our kids were moving on.

"When we decided to move back to England, I gave my wife the choice of where she wanted to live because she'd been following me around for so long.

"The natural one was either the West Midlands, where we're both from and our families are from, or Preston and the north west area because of our relationships and how we felt here - and she chose to come back here, which I was hoping she would say.

The Lilywhites return to league action after the three-week international break with a home game against Millwall on Saturday, 10 October.

Alexander, who has never managed in the Championship before, said his arrival gave the players a chance to "restart" at the club and that he was "not going to drag anything forward".

He said the extra time he will have to work with the group before a first competitive match will be important as he looks to turn their fortunes around.

"When I've took over a couple of other clubs mid-season it's been late in the week, it's been Thursday or Friday and then a game, so to have a full two weeks working with them is valuable to us but the proof will be in the pudding when we play Millwall," he said.

"It's important because there are certain things we really believe in and commit to so a two-week window to implement those things will be good but it will take longer than that to be the full team we are."

articles.title: Turkiye arrests president, six members of football refereeing body in probe
articles.summary: Arrests were made over interference with refereeing procedures, among other accusations, Turkish justice minister says.
articles.body:
The head of Turkiye’s football refereeing body and six other people have been arrested over accusations of interference in refereeing procedures, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said.

“Claims regarding interference in the formation of referee classifications, assignments, scoring and appointment processes, as well as rule examinations, have been investigated,” Gurlek wrote in a social media post on Tuesday.

Ferhat Gundogdu, the president of the refereeing body, and his deputy were among those arrested.

Gurlek said searches had been carried out at the suspects’ “residences, workplaces and offices”.

“We will steadfastly continue the fight for clean football so that claims undermining trust in Turkish football are clarified, those responsible are held accountable before the law, and football is remembered for the effort, struggle, and sportsmanship on the field,” Gurlek added.

A year ago, the Turkish Football Federation (TFF) suspended 149 referees on charges of involvement in an illegal betting scandal .

The TFF investigation found that 371 out of the country’s 571 referees officiating in the professional leagues had betting accounts and 152 of them actively placed bets.

Some 29 people were arrested in the sprawling scandal, including 14 footballers, one of whom was Fenerbahce’s international midfielder Mert Hakan Yandas.

Authorities suspended more than 1,000 players, including 25 from the first division.

However, Gurlek did not draw any link between last year’s betting scandal and the current investigation.

articles.title: Man City’s Premier League charges: What’s the latest and what comes next?
articles.summary: Swingeing sanctions against City for breaching financial fair play rules would send shockwaves through English football.
articles.body:
Manchester City’s fate in a legal battle with the Premier League is yet to be sealed, but reports that it has been found guilty of widespread financial misconduct have led to speculation about what comes next.

As the dominant Premier League force for more than a decade, City would face swingeing sanctions that would send shockwaves through English football.

Rival clubs are set to launch their own legal action seeking hundreds of millions of pounds in compensation, while there is debate over whether some of City’s many titles and trophies over the past 15 years could be stripped.

City, which has always denied any wrongdoing, has pledged to clear its name.

So what is the latest reaction to the case and what is likely to come next?

The Athletic first reported on Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges it faced.

However, no sanction has yet been approved.

Even once a decision is made on how City will be punished, should it be found guilty, the club is almost certain to appeal.

In a letter to fans on Saturday, City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said: “Our confidence and intent in proving the club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.”

A case that began after German outlet Der Spiegel published leaked documents from City executives in 2018 could still take a long time to fully resolve.

According to Premier League rules, the sanctions can vary from a points deduction to a fine or even expulsion from the division.

Everton and Nottingham Forest were handed points deductions in the 2023-24 season for single breaches of financial sustainability rules. On that basis, City would face almost certain relegation if found guilty of more than 100 charges.

Whether the sanction is applied before an appeal is heard will be another bone of contention.

If it is, City could face relegation before overturning any guilty verdict.

On the other hand, if City, who currently sit top of the table, are not punished until after an appeal, it could cost other clubs their place in the top-flight or lucrative European qualification.

Even after the Premier League process is over, there is also the chance that City’s Abu Dhabi-backed owners will seek redress in England’s High Court if they challenge a legal issue regarding how the arbitration process was conducted.

City’s rivals were quick to revel in the news of the club’s potential demise.

“Another Premier League medal to be added to the cabinet,” posted former Manchester United defender Rio Ferdinand, who was part of the United team to finish second to City in the 2011-12 season.

The reality is that stripping and retroactively awarding titles is a messy process.

The charges against City relate to the period between 2009 and 2018. During that time, they won four league titles, with United and Liverpool twice finishing second in those seasons.

Yet City have won another four since, arguably built on foundations that were fraudulently gained.

They also won four League Cups and one FA Cup, the club’s first trophy in 35 years, between 2009 and 2018.

“I don’t seriously believe any other trophies and titles will be handed back over either,” Tony Pulis, whose side Stoke lost the 2011 FA Cup final to City, told the BBC.

“A points deduction and a massive fine feels far more likely. But I still feel cheated.”

Former Tottenham Hotspur ‌manager Mauricio Pochettino expressed sadness at City being found ⁠guilty of breaching ⁠financial rules, saying that if true, it would confirm “a period of deception” in the sport.

“Whatever punishment [they choose], it’s impossible to turn back time. It’s done a lot of damage,” Pochettino, now coach of ‌the US men’s team, told reporters on Monday.

“At the end of the day, many clubs followed the rules, and some didn’t … What are they going to do? An economic punishment? Docking points? It’s really hard. It’s sad.”

La Liga president Javier Tebas said City should face the “most severe sanction” available if it has breached financial regulations.

The Spaniard, speaking at a football performance and health summit in London on Tuesday, said he had been raising concerns about City since 2017.

“To have been breaking the rules for more than 10 years, however minor the breaches may have been, is very serious,” he said.

“So there has to be a severe punishment for breaking the rules, not just to set an example, but because the rules were broken.”

“What has happened is very important, and hopefully it will be a before-and-after moment, not just in the Premier League but in European football as well, because the Manchester effect was an effect across all of Europe,” Tebas added.

Addressing the European Football Clubs board on Monday, Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano ⁠said the club would do everything to clear its name.

The procedure would take years before reaching a conclusion, ⁠a source familiar with the discussions told the Reuters news agency.

Soriano, who sits on EFC’s board, also declined to comment to reporters on City being found guilty of 114 of 115 alleged breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, according to media reports confirmed to Reuters by a source ‌familiar with the situation.

Less than a month ago, City completed the biggest-ever transfer spend in one window, splashing out about 460 million pounds ($347m) on the likes of Enzo Fernandez, Elliott Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The impending verdict on the charges has, to this point, made little impact on City’s ability to attract and retain its top names.

Talismanic striker Erling Haaland signed a nine-year contract in 2025 that could keep him tied down till his 34th birthday.

How many, if any, of the players managed to negotiate exit clauses if City were heavily sanctioned remains to be seen.

articles.title: Ya hay precios para el Clásico del Spotify Camp Nou: no son asequibles
articles.standfirst: El Barça ya ha puesto a la venta las primeras entradas, exclusivamente para socios
articles.summary: El Barça ya ha puesto a la venta las primeras entradas, exclusivamente para socios
articles.body: Ya falta menos de un mes para el primer Clásico de la temporada 26-27. Ha comenzado la cuenta atrás. El Barcelona recibe al Real Madrid en el Spotify Camp Nou el próximo 25 de octubre a las 21:00 horas, y el club catalán ya ha puesto algunas entradas a la venta. De momento, hay tickets disponibles sólo para sus socios. Todos, a precios más que destacados. El Barça permite un primer plazo de preventa exclusivo para socios (tienen un cinco por ciento de descuento), que arrancó hoy, ya está habilitada la compra en los canales oficiales del club catalán, y se prolongará durante 48 horas. El método de transacción que utiliza el Barcelona apuesta por la movilidad de los precios ya que se modula en función de la oferta y la demanda y del número de localidades disponibles en cada zona del campo. Así que, en estos momentos, la entrada más asequible tiene un coste de 476,50 euros, y corresponde a la zona Gol 1. En el Córner 1, el precio de los billetes ya se eleva hasta los 699 euros; en el Lateral 2 Superior su coste sube hasta los 799 euros; en Tribuna 2 Superior se sitúa en 899... El asiento más caro de este tramo alcanza los 999: pertenecen a Tribuna 2 Inferior y Tribuna 1. También hay entradas VIP Premium a partir de 1.750 euros, que incluyen acceso a las zonas VIP, catering... En cualquier caso y a pesar de los elevados precios de los billetes, el Barça está seguro de que habrá lleno en el Clásico del Spotify Camp Nou. La expectación es ya máxima. El arranque histórico de temporada de los de Flick invita al optimismo a la afición culé en el regreso de Mourinho a un Clásico.

articles.title: Why Salisbury FC are 'bigger than many Premier League teams' in Kuwait
articles.summary: Sixth-tier Salisbury FC have a unique relationship with Kuwait, where they are regarded as "bigger than many Premier League" clubs.
articles.body:
As with every home game, the Salisbury FC players and coaching staff went to embrace the fans in the Andrews Terrace at The Ray Mac Stadium after Saturday's 2-0 win against Folkestone Invicta.

Alongside the normal applause and cheers, they were greeted with a chant that isn't a regular from the songbook.

"Kuwait away ole, ole," sang fans of the National League South outfit.

The players clapped back with an extra buzz - within 24 hours they would be travelling to the Middle East.

"Straight away we all said, 'yeah, we're all in," explains Salisbury player Luke Russe.

"It's a unique opportunity and as players, we are so thankful to everybody involved in making this trip happen. I've been involved in this level for a long time now and I've never had an experience like it."

The five-day trip involves the club facing one of Kuwait's most successful teams on Wednesday, Al Qadsia, who have won more than 50 trophies, before returning on Thursday to play Saturday's FA Cup third qualifying round against Dulwich Hamlet.

It comes as part of the club's continued link with Kuwait through their owner Ali Alhamad, who purchased the club in 2025.

The club hopes the trip will offer significant commercial growth and, for the players, an opportunity to experience football in a new environment and culture.

The Mohammad Al-Hamad Stadium holds 22,000 spectators, more than five times that of Salisbury's The Ray Mac.

"We'd love to win the game," says Russe. "But at the same time I think it's more about the experience and about the club as a whole, going over there, living that way of life and experiencing the game.

"We've got a very young group, so for them to experience that and kind of experience cultures and differences is great.

"It'll be a fantastic opportunity for us players, for the staff, and I think it'll bring the whole club even closer to what we are now."

The players will get to visit local restaurants, try local food and coffee, visit schools and universities, and hold a question and answer session for locals to understand how an English football club operates from the perspective of owner Alhamad.

"It will help the players themselves with opening up their horizons into different cultures, different countries, experiencing other footballing nations and other styles of football," he says.

The country's interest in Salisbury is evident.

Four of the club's sponsors are from Kuwait, including the front of shirt sponsor for a company that created the country's first Sharia-compliant digital bank, and the training kit represents a popular Acai company that can only be bought in Kuwait.

On Instagram the official Arabic account of Salisbury FC has more than 14,000 followers - only slightly fewer than their official English profile.

When the squad arrived in Kuwait they were greeted by a small group of fans, while school children interacted with them as if they were Premier League players.

"I would even go further than saying that Salisbury in Kuwait is bigger than many of the Premier League teams in the UK," says Alhamad.

"So I am not exaggerating when I do say that it is a huge name in Kuwait but what's more important than the size is we are contributing a lot to the local community here in Kuwait and to the children and the future of the football in Kuwait.

"Salisbury really is an integral part of opening those avenues and helping the youth here to be better in all the aspects we're looking for."

The eagerness the players showed shocked Alhamad, with all of the squad, except Jaiden Bartolo who is on international duty, agreeing to go within an hour.

Along with the cultural experience, the club is also using this as a way to grow financially, with all ticket sales and advertisement money going to Salisbury.

Meanwhile, Salisbury have set up a summer camp in the country and ran a trial session where the top three players trained with the first team during pre-season.

"It's quite simple in my mind. If you do what other people do, you'll just get the same results everyone else does," says Alhamad.

"Football in England, especially in the non-league, is a brutal business. So just throwing in money to the football club with the aim of getting promotion is fool's gold, in my opinion.

"The right way to do it is to build it properly all the way from the bottom and if you just limit yourself to one market, which is the city or town that you are in, that is pretty limited.

"With social media and the avenues we have, such as being in Kuwait and the Gulf and Arab regions. That's a huge untapped market that is thirsty for English football."

People in Kuwait are avid watchers of the Premier League but non-league is still very much an unknown commodity in the country.

"People are not properly educated in the fact that the non-league is actually a really high quality and that is also an indirect goal of mine with this match," he adds.

"We're here to show them, you're belittling, playing the sixth tier of English football, the second step of the English non-league.

"We'll show you what we have and you never know, maybe the sixth tier of English football will beat the top tier on the biggest team in Kuwait.

This growth in Kuwait will offer Salisbury FC an important opportunity that is rare for a National League South team.

But ensuring The Whites remain strongly embedded within the local community in the city will also be vital, with the FA Cup on Saturday the first test on their return.

"I have grown to love it and love the people of Salisbury and the towns around it," says Alhamad.

"It's a great place to be. And that's what I'm really focusing on not just in a trip here in Kuwait, also in our heart and soul, our fans, our community, which is Salisbury."

articles.title: 'Terapia Ancelotti' para Vinicius
articles.standfirst: El brasileño reencontró el gol con la Canarinha en la remontada ante Australia, y recibió el respaldo público de un Ancelotti que le cedió el penalti para devolverle la confianza
articles.summary: El brasileño reencontró el gol con la Canarinha en la remontada ante Australia, y recibió el respaldo público de un Ancelotti que le cedió el penalti para devolverle la confianza
articles.body: Vinicius está en plena búsqueda de sí mismo. No solo del gol, que por fin ha vuelto a celebrar ante Australia, sino también de ese fútbol desacomplejado que un día lo aupó a la cima. El brasileño llevaba desde agosto sin ver puerta, poco más de un mes que se le ha hecho eterno, y su condición de intocable en el Real Madrid ha quedado más en entredicho que nunca. Los buenos minutos de Diomande en su banda han obligado a replantear un estatus que parecía incuestionable. A ese cuestionamiento se ha sumado un rendimiento por debajo de lo esperado a las órdenes de Mourinho, que el Bernabéu ha castigado en más de una ocasión con pitos dirigidos a él. La combinación ha instalado al extremo en un momento delicado, de esos de los que solo se sale por la única puerta que un futbolista de su pedigrí reconoce: la del gol. Y esa puerta, esta vez, se abrió lejos de Chamartín. Fue en este parón de selecciones, largo en su doble acepción. Largo por las tres semanas de compromisos, y largo por las distancias que Brasil debe recorrer para cumplir con una gira que le ha llevado a medirse a Australia y que le enfrentará también a la India. Más de 30.000 kilómetros y 50 horas de vuelo. El primer paso lo dio Vinicius desde los once metros, un gol que sirvió para calmar las aguas de un partido embarrado y para desenquistar a la Canarinha de Ancelotti tras un Mundial que se quedó muy por debajo de las expectativas. El propio seleccionador abrigó a su pupilo y le recetó confianza. "Conozco muy bien a Vinicius. Es un jugador fundamental para Brasil, lo ha sido en mi historia futbolística y lo seguirá siendo en el futuro de la selección", proclamó Ancelotti. "Es cierto que no está en su mejor momento, pero aun así puede marcar diferencias, y es lo que ha hecho hoy: crea nuestro tercer gol y luego lo transforma de penalti". Y remató, por si quedaba alguna duda: "Tengo paciencia con Vinicius porque él se lo merece". Detrás de aquel penalti hubo ensayo y error. Carletto quiso que lo lanzara el propio Vinicius, a diferencia de lo ocurrido en el Mundial ante Noruega, cuando la pena máxima recayó en Bruno Guimaraes, que la falló con el marcador aún en tablas en un duelo que acabó con Brasil eliminado. El técnico, esta vez, priorizó devolverle la confianza al extremo antes que cualquier otra consideración. Guimaraes también desveló el gesto que se escondía tras la jugada. "Bruno es quien lanza los penaltis cuando Raphinha no está, y yo pensaba tirarlo, pero él sabe que estoy necesitando un poco de confianza, que llevaba partidos sin marcar", relató Vinicius. Su compañero lo confirmó sin asomo de reproche: "Aquí no hay ninguna vanidad. En el último partido del Mundial, Ancelotti me mandó tirar a mí; hoy se lo mandó a Vini, que también necesitaba marcar. Queremos el bien de Brasil. Feliz por él". Ahora, con el gol ya en el zurrón y el respaldo de su seleccionador como aval, Vinicius encara el reto de trasladar esa inyección de moral al día a día del Real Madrid. El mimo de Ancelotti ha sido el primer bálsamo; el verdadero examen, sin embargo, le espera en Chamartín, donde deberá reconquistar a la grada y afianzar su puesto. El camino de vuelta ya tiene un primer paso dado.

articles.title: Al Khelaifi: "Es triste ver lo que está pasando"
articles.standfirst: El presidente de la EFC agradece a Laporta su vuelta a la organización, a Florentino que esté "a punto de hacerlo" y pide a Aleksander Ceferin que se presente de nuevo a las elecciones
articles.summary: El presidente de la EFC agradece a Laporta su vuelta a la organización, a Florentino que esté "a punto de hacerlo" y pide a Aleksander Ceferin que se presente de nuevo a las elecciones
articles.body: Nasser al Khelaifi ha ofrecido su discurso en la Asamblea de la Asociación de clubes europeos (EFC) en el que ha agradecido a Joan Laporta su esfuerzo por devolver al Barcelona al grupo de clubes europeos que ya superan los 850 miembros y también a Florentino Pérez por trabajar ya en llegar a un acuerdo que plasmará al Real Madrid como un miembro más. Ya hay conversaciones y, pese a que Anas Laghari ha acudido hoy a Copenhague como representante de A22, la sociedad que iba a explotar la Superliga, su presencia es un síntoma de la mejora de relaciones entre la EFC y el club blanco. Según fuentes próximas a A22, el acuerdo para que el Madrid regrese a la asociación está cerca y será entonces cuando el club blanco retire su demanda millonaria. "Me gustaría dar las gracias al presidente del FC Barcelona, Joan Laporta, por su confianza en la EFC: bienvenido de nuevo a la familia. También me gustaría dar las gracias al presidente del Real Madrid CF, Florentino Pérez, por creer que el futuro del fútbol europeo debe construirse sobre la base de la unidad y los intereses colectivos; y nos complace que estén a punto de reincorporarse a la familia de los Clubes de Fútbol Europeos", comentó el presidente del PSG. El presidente de la EFC, sin mencionar a Gianni Infantino, apeló a la unidad para seguir adelante y evitar guerras como la que está sucediendo ahora mismo tras el intento fallido del presidente de la FIFA de privatizar el Mundial por la puerta de atrás. "El fútbol mundial también es muy importante para nuestros clubes. Todos vimos la Copa del Mundo de la FIFA 2026 este verano: 857 jugadores procedían de clubes europeos, lo que supone casi el 70 % del total de jugadores y el equivalente a la composición de 33 de las 48 selecciones. Espero que la gente vea por fin el valor de los clubes", apuntó. "Es realmente triste ver la situación actual, -denunció el presidente del PSG-. En lugar de mejorar nuestro deporte, estamos perdiendo el tiempo lidiando con problemas y dificultades. El fútbol funciona cuando nos escuchamos unos a otros. Cuando somos transparentes entre nosotros. Pero, sobre todo, cuando somos honestos. Y sean cuales sean nuestras diferencias, el fútbol es más grande y más importante que cualquiera de nosotros", comentó.. El presidente de la EFC animó a presentarse a Aleksander Ceferin a las elecciones, algo que debe anunciar el próximo mes de diciembre, cuatro meses antes del Congreso que en abril de 2027 tendrá lugar en Kazajistán: "Cuando la UEFA y los clubes trabajan codo con codo, el fútbol sale ganando. Cualquier cuestión, cualquier problema: los abordamos cara a cara. A veces, la UEFA no está contenta con los clubes. A veces, los clubes no están contentos con la UEFA. Pero encontramos soluciones". Hoy en día, -añadió Al Khelaifi- 36 representantes del EFC forman parte de 15 comisiones de la UEFA: eso es una verdadera colaboración. No puedo hablar de la UEFA sin mencionar a su presidente. Aleksander, sé que estás harto de mis llamadas y mensajes diarios con todas nuestras peticiones como clubes. Tengo que darte las gracias por tu paciencia, por apoyar a los clubes y por defender lo mejor para el fútbol, incluso cuando no es fácil. El fútbol necesita grandes líderes como tú y, en nombre de los más de 900 clubes de la EFC, te pedimos que te presentes de nuevo a la presidencia el año que viene". "A medida que nuestra membresía crece y evoluciona, nuestra gobernanza y nuestras estructuras también deben cambiar. El EFC de hoy no es la ECA de ayer. Por eso votaremos hoy mismo para modificar nuestros estatutos aún más. Esto significará que todos los miembros —ordinarios y asociados; pequeños, medianos y grandes— tendrán voz y voto directos en todas las decisiones importantes del EFC. Seremos más democráticos que nunca —en nuestra Junta Directiva, grupos de trabajo y comités—, pero sin perder nuestra eficacia ni nuestro equilibrio. Todos los miembros podrán representar a la EFC en la UEFA, la FIFA y otros comités; y contaremos con una sólida representación femenina garantizada en todas las subdivisiones de la Junta Directiva. Un modelo de buena representación y buena gobernanza", añadió. Nasser al Khelaifi insiste en que la EFC va a seguir creciendo: "Recuerdo cuando, hace unos años, dije por primera vez que deberíamos ampliar nuestra afiliación y fijarnos como objetivo llegar a los 1.000 clubes afiliados. Algunos me dijeron: '¿Te has vuelto loco?'. Otros dijeron: 'Es imposible'. Pero nuestro recorrido nos ha enseñado que nuestra diversidad no es un problema; no es nuestra debilidad. Es nuestra fortaleza. Es nuestro superpoder. Un club con 5.000 aficionados puede enseñar algo a un club con 50 millones de aficionados. Un club femenino de Irlanda puede inspirar a un club masculino de Italia. Una academia juvenil aquí en Dinamarca puede formar a un jugador que cambie el fútbol en todo el mundo", añadió.

articles.title: Nation's Longest Active HSFB Winning Streak Ends After Massapequa's Upset vs. Garden City
articles.summary: A New York high school football game Monday night proved to have national implications.
articles.body:
A New York high school football game Monday night proved to have national implications.

The Massapequa Chiefs beat the Garden City Trojans 21-14. Garden City's 68-game winning streak, which had been the longest in the country, is no more. USA Today 's Joseph Spears noted the Trojans last lost in 2019.

NFL head coach regrets reaction to dirty hit

Massapequa senior wide receiver Dylan Milio scored the game-winning touchdown inside the final minute. An interception by defensive lineman Ryan Chabus set up the pivotal drive.

"It was definitely one of the closest games we've ever played in," he told the New York Post 's Alex Mitchell . "It meant a little more because now we could break history. In school, we were not really paying attention to teachers today, honestly."

The longest winning streak in high school football now belongs to Carl Albert High School in Midwest City, Oklahoma. The Titans have reeled off 58 victories in a row.

Setting the all-time record will only require Carl Albert to almost triple its ongoing run. De La Salle High School in California famously won 151 straight games between 1992 and 2004.

articles.title: Sevilla homenajea a la selección ante la Copa del Mundo
articles.standfirst: El Parlamento de Andalucía acoge la segunda estrella en vísperas del duelo ante Croacia en el Sánchez-Pizjuán
articles.summary: El Parlamento de Andalucía acoge la segunda estrella en vísperas del duelo ante Croacia en el Sánchez-Pizjuán
articles.body: Este martes, el Parlamento de Andalucía se vistió de gala para protagonizar un acto institucional en homenaje a la selección española de fútbol. La Cámara autonómica recibió la Copa del Mundo conquistada el pasado verano en Estados Unidos, en un evento marcado por el arraigo histórico del combinado nacional en la región. El trofeo llegó en Sevilla el domingo y permanecerá en la capital hispalense hasta mañana miércoles, en el marco de la gira 'Reyes del mundo' organizada por la RFEF tras arrancar en Málaga. El evento ha desatado una fiebre colectiva, pues en los últimos días el recinto parlamentario ha registrado más de 6.000 visitas de aficionados deseosos de fotografiarse con la Copa del Mundo. Esta cita sirve como antesala del duelo que la selección española disputará esta noche ante Croacia en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, correspondiente a la fase de grupos de la Liga de Naciones y que supone el partido número 90 de la Roja en Andalucía en sus más de cien años de historia. Durante el acto se puso de manifiesto el impacto que ha tenido el segundo mundial masculino del fútbol español. La presidenta del Parlamento andaluz, Ana Mestre, abrió la ronda de intervenciones destacando la trascendencia del triunfo: "La selección española son valores civiles y democráticos que aúnan los sentimientos más profundos de sacrificio, convivencia y deportividad. La responsabilidad de estos jugadores es inmensa, pues son referentes de muchos, pero principalmente de gran parte de los jóvenes". Además, quiso añadir: "Si recordamos el partido con Argentina, creo que esos valores que ahí se demostraron dicen lo que son los jugadores de España y también lo que somos los españoles y españolas". El presidente de la Real Federación Andaluza de Fútbol (RFAF), Pedro Curtido, incidió en el marco autonómico y la cohesión social: "Es un honor estar aquí con la Copa del Mundo en este espacio que representa la convivencia y la identidad de los andaluces. Es un orgullo aún más grande ver el respeto, los valores, la unión y la cohesión con los que esta selección ha dado un ejemplo al mundo con su comportamiento en el pasado Mundial". Curtido también se mostró tajante respecto al futuro próximo: "Seguro que Andalucía tendrá un papel muy importante en el Mundial 2030. Ilusionaremos al país y a los andaluces para que seamos una referencia a nivel de capacidad hotelera, gastronomía, playas, clima o conexiones aéreas". El presidente de la RFEF, Rafael Louzán, recalcó el acierto de elegir Sevilla para el reencuentro de la selección con su gente: "Todo este periplo no se puede hacer en otro mejor sitio que en Andalucía. A pesar de que yo soy de Galicia -y si va allí seguro que la vamos a recibir muy bien-, el primer partido de la selección después de ser doble campeona del mundo tenía que ser en Andalucía y en esta maravillosa ciudad de Sevilla, porque es el hogar de la selección española de fútbol". El máximo responsable de la federación confesó que "esta planificación se hizo previamente a ganar el Mundial, por tanto, teníamos expectativas de que podíamos ser campeones". Louzán elogió el modelo futbolístico y el factor humano del grupo: "En este Mundial ha ganado el fútbol sobre todo por la forma, ganando con humildad, sencillez y mucha naturalidad. En cada país que visitamos nos lo agradecen porque España ha marcado un estilo. La selección es el elemento de cohesión más importante que tiene este país. Ha hecho posible que este país viva un momento que vamos a recordar muchísimos años, igual que lo fue en el año 2010 en Sudáfrica. Esta victoria en Nueva York va a quedar marcada para muchos niños". Asimismo, Louzán subrayó la época dorada que atraviesa el fútbol español: "Dominamos el fútbol en el ámbito masculino y femenino, doblemente campeones del mundo. Somos campeones de Europa en fútbol sala masculino y en fútbol playa masculino y femenino. No hay ninguna federación que atesore un año como este. Te preguntan por muchos países cómo se consigue. Lo hablábamos en la ciudad deportiva del Sevilla con Joaquín Caparrós, sevillano insigne que está atravesando un momento difícil. Nos decía que el tesoro más importante es la formación que saben aplicar nuestros entrenadores. Por tanto, hay que reconocer ese trabajo que hacen en todos los rincones de España". Cerró el evento el presidente de la Junta de Andalucía, Juanma Moreno, que enfatizó la expectación desatada en la sede parlamentaria: "Desde el 20 de febrero del año 2003 que inauguraron sus majestades los Reyes, Don Juan Carlos y Doña Sofía, este Parlamento de Andalucía, hemos tenido insignes visitantes. Pero ninguna visita ha causado tanta expectación, felicidad y presencia social como la Copa del Mundo. Es un anhelo colectivo, el sueño de casi 50 millones de españoles que deseamos siempre ser campeones en un deporte que para nosotros es el deporte rey, que se practica en las calles, en los patios, en las plazas de los pueblos, donde más federados hay". Moreno puso en valor el ciclo victorioso que vive la Roja: "Estamos ante un momento muy dulce que debemos aprovechar, saborear y disfrutar porque en el fútbol como en la vida no todo siempre sale bien". Igualmente, ensalzó las raíces andaluzas dentro del vestuario nacional y la pasión de la grada hispalense: "Me siento muy orgulloso de la comunión, el vínculo afectivo, emocional e histórico que tiene Andalucía y Sevilla con la selección española. Jugar en Sevilla siempre aporta un plus de motivación, ilusión y alegría que genera a través del público". Para concluir, Moreno agradeció el impacto social de este hito deportivo: "El fútbol es un paréntesis feliz que nos alegra a todos. Me siento muy orgulloso de ver cómo en ese magnífico plantel hay andaluces como Fabián y Gavi de los Palacios y Villafranca, y Álex Baena de Roquetas de Mar". El presidente autonómico remató el acto recordando el valor de la cita en el Sánchez-Pizjuán: "Es la primera vez que la selección española después de proclamarse campeona del mundo, viene a suelo patrio y lo hace en el sur, en Sevilla y en un estadio talismán, con un lleno y con el calor y el cariño de toda Andalucía".

articles.title: ‘The emperor is naked’: UEFA’s Ceferin takes aim at FIFA boss Infantino
articles.summary: UEFA slams Infantino over his aborted plan to sell off stakes in FIFA competitions to private investors.
articles.body:
UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin said “the emperor is naked” in a blistering attack on FIFA President Gianni Infantino and his failed plan to sell a stake ⁠in the governing body’s commercial rights to private investors.

Addressing the European Football Clubs General Assembly in Copenhagen on Tuesday, Ceferin invoked Hans Christian Andersen’s The Emperor’s New Clothes as he criticised the language FIFA had used to defend Infantino’s ⁠shelved FIFA Forward Enterprise project .

“Almost 200 years ago, he [Andersen] wrote The Emperor’s New Clothes,” Ceferin said.

“We all know the story. An emperor is persuaded that he is wearing magnificent clothes, clothes which he is told only the foolish or unfit cannot see.

“His court goes along with it until a child simply says aloud what everybody can see. The ‌emperor is naked.”

Infantino’s FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal would have created a FIFA-controlled commercial subsidiary holding rights to competitions including the men’s and women’s World Cups and Club World Cup and allowed private investors to acquire up to 20 percent of the entity.

Infantino had promoted the proposal as a way to generate more money for “football development” and said it was subject to “democratic consultation” with FIFA’s 211 member associations before it was abandoned following widespread opposition.

Ceferin directly challenged that language.

“Perhaps the moral of ⁠the story is convenient words cannot change uncomfortable realities,” he said.

“Now world football ⁠has heard some very convenient words recently. ‘Development’, ‘democratisation’, ‘consultation’, words used in fact to describe the opposite.

“Selling part of football’s future does not become development because you say it’s ‘development’.

“Putting a fait accompli in front of national associations does not mean democratisation, even ⁠if you call it ‘democratisation’. However big the cheque is.

“And secrecy does not become consultation because you call it ‘consultation’.”

Ceferin then asked club executives to imagine one ⁠of their senior officials secretly negotiating away control of their “crown jewels” without ⁠the knowledge of their board, players or supporters, with the deal almost completed by the time they learned of it.

He went on to refer to a hypothetical situation in which the same person created an award for a politician and, ‌soon afterwards, the politician made a phone call after which “the rules are not the same any more.”

“How many times would this have to happen at your clubs before the world says ‘enough’?” Ceferin said.

“Well, my friends, I think ‌it’s ‌time to say enough.”

He ended the passage by accusing unnamed decision-makers of bending rules when they became inconvenient, excluding those who were supposed to have a say and treating football’s future as “just another bargaining chip.”

articles.title: El Málaga encuentra motivos para creer
articles.standfirst: El 42% de los equipos que llegaron a la séptima jornada de Liga sin ganar lograron salvarse
articles.summary: El 42% de los equipos que llegaron a la séptima jornada de Liga sin ganar lograron salvarse
articles.body: El Málaga ha cerrado las siete primeras jornadas de Liga sin conocer la victoria. El equipo de Juanfran Funes suma tres empates y cuatro derrotas, un inicio que ya ha llevado a parte de la afición a hacer cuentas por la permanencia. Los precedentes de las últimas dos décadas muestran que la situación es complicada, aunque también existen ejemplos de equipos que consiguieron darle la vuelta. En total, 33 equipos llegaron a la séptima jornada sin ganar en lo que llevamos. Catorce terminaron salvándose, un 42% de los casos. El último fue el Celta de la 2025-26. El Getafe en tres ocasiones (2024-25, 2021-22 en la que no había logrado ni siquiera un punto, y 2007-08), el Almería (2013-14), el Espanyol (2012-13), el Athletic Club (2011-12), el Zaragoza en dos temporadas (2010-11 y 2000-01), el Villarreal (2009-10), Osasuna (2008-09), el Espanyol (2003-04), el Rayo Vallecano y la Real Sociedad (ambos en la 2001-02) tampoco habían estrenado el casillero de victorias en las primeras siete citas ligueras y acabaron salvándose al término de la temporada. El caso más espectacular es el de los azulones no lograron su primera victoria hasta la octava jornada y, tras la destitución de Míchel y la llegada de Quique Sánchez Flores, consiguieron remontar el vuelo para acabar decimoquintos. Es el único equipo de la historia en llegar con 0 puntos a esta jornada y acabar logrando la permanencia. Antes hubo otros cuatro casos. El primero fue el Villarreal de la 2009-10, que arrancó con tres empates y cuatro derrotas, exactamente el mismo balance que presenta ahora el Málaga. Su primera victoria llegó en la octava jornada, precisamente ante el conjunto blanquiazul. El equipo amarillo terminó séptimo y logró clasificarse para la Europa League. En la 2010-11, el Zaragoza tampoco ganó en sus siete primeros partidos y llegó a esa jornada con solo tres puntos. Los maños no consiguieron su primera victoria hasta la décima fecha, pero una gran segunda vuelta y cuatro triunfos en las seis últimas jornadas, incluido un 2-3 en el Santiago Bernabéu, les permitieron salvarse. También lo consiguió el Espanyol en la temporada 2012-13. Con solo dos puntos en las siete primeras jornadas, el conjunto perico cambió su dinámica tras la salida de Mauricio Pochettino y la llegada de Javier Aguirre. Terminó decimotercero y logró la permanencia con margen. Un año después fue el Almería quien protagonizó otra remontada. Los rojiblancos llegaron a la séptima jornada sin ganar, pero encadenaron después tres victorias consecutivas. Terminaron décimos séptimos, con 40 puntos, y aseguraron la permanencia tras no perder ninguno de sus cuatro últimos encuentros. Los precedentes negativos son mayoría. De esos 19 equipos que llegaron a la séptima jornada sin ganar, 14 terminaron descendiendo. En esa lista aparecen Real Sociedad, Levante —en tres ocasiones—, Sporting de Gijón, Racing de Santander, Córdoba, Osasuna, Málaga, Leganés, Huesca, Elche, Almería y Las Palmas. El Málaga ya sabe lo que significa afrontar este escenario. En la temporada 2017-18, el conjunto blanquiazul tampoco consiguió ganar ninguno de sus siete primeros partidos y acabó descendiendo a Segunda División. Casi una década después, el equipo de Funes vuelve a encontrarse ante un inicio estadísticamente poco habitual. Los precedentes no condenan al Málaga, pero sí dejan clara la necesidad de encontrar cuanto antes una primera victoria que cambie la dinámica.

articles.standfirst: Miguel Ángel Gil Marín y Joan Laporta charlaron de forma cordial en la Asamblea de la Asociación de Clubes Europeos tras un verano más que movido entre ambos clubes
articles.summary: Miguel Ángel Gil Marín y Joan Laporta charlaron de forma cordial en la Asamblea de la Asociación de Clubes Europeos tras un verano más que movido entre ambos clubes
articles.body: La Asamblea de la Asociación de clubes europeos que se celebra en Copenhague El Atlético de Madrid y el Barça no viven la mejor relación institucional desde hace un tiempo. Es un secreto a voces y no hay más que volver al verano tan movido por el caso Julián Álvarez, algo que para el club rojiblanco no olvida por ahora. Hay por tanto mucho camino por recorrer aún para que las cosas vuelvan a la normalidad, pero Copenhague podría ser el primer punto de encuentro para, al menos, ir destensando la relación entre ambos clubes. Miguel Ángel Gil, en representación del club rojiblanco y como miembro del Comité Ejecutivo de la EFC (Asociación de clubes europeos), coincidió con Laporta y a ambos se les vio charlar de forma cordial. Al menos para la labor por el fútbol europeo, parecen condenados a entenderse. Después de las duras palabras que el consejero delegado ha tenido a lo largo del verano hacia el FC Barcelona y su presidente, Gil Marín comentó antes de abandonar el congreso de la EFC que “la educación, las formas y el respeto están por encima de las diferencias que podamos tener entre ambos clubes, eso no ha cambiado”. Sin embargo, es evidente que el regreso del Barcelona a la EFC casi obliga a remar en algunos casos en el mismo sentido. No hay que olvidar que Gil Marín fue clave para el regreso del Barcelona a la asociación de clubes europeos después del proyecto de la Superliga europea, junto al Real Madrid: ”Es importante para el fútbol español que el Barcelona esté presente en este foro junto al resto de clubes para que todos trabajemos de la mano por un mejor futuro para el sector”, añadió el dirigente rojiblanco.

Oregon head coach Dan Lanning doesn't have time for USC's juice box celebration.

In a video posted by Oregon featuring Lanning delivering a message in practice leading up to the showdown between the Big Ten rivals (starts at 2:00 mark), the Ducks coach dismissed the juice boxes because "it's a fake energy" that "ain't real."
