Lanning used the juice boxes to explain how the Trojans create their energy on the field. USC broke out a big "juice box" during its season-opening win over San Jose State.

They have remained a staple on the Trojans' sidelines since then. Head coach Lincoln Riley told reporters on Sept. 8 that players did feel a boost from having them around.

"The energy on our sidelines is real," Riley said. "You feel that from our guys. Our team feels it. No matter what atmosphere we play in — whether it's home, whether it's on the road, no matter how the game's going, our mindset is that we bring our own energy wherever we play."

Unfortunately, the juice may have run out of the boxes at some point during Saturday's game. Oregon earned a 41-27 victory at the Coliseum, handing the Trojans their first home loss since Nov. 30, 2024.

It was a much-needed win for an Oregon team that looked sluggish to start the season, including a 39-31 loss to Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. A second loss would have left it a huge climb to get back into playoff contention.

articles.title: Dan Lanning Blasts 'Cheap' Hit on Dante Moore as New Video Reveals Oregon HC's Real-Time Reaction
articles.summary: Oregon football's official X account posted a video Tuesday showing head coach Dan Lanning's reaction to the hit that knocked quarterback Dante Moore out of Saturday's game against USC.
articles.body:
Oregon football's official X account posted a video Tuesday showing head coach Dan Lanning's reaction to the hit that knocked quarterback Dante Moore out of Saturday's game against USC.

Beginning at the nine-minute mark of the video, Lanning is shown addressing the hit with his team, saying, "You saw that s--t was cheap. ... The best thing we can do is go fight for our f--king brother, you with me?"

Lanning then led his team in a prayer for Moore before adding, "Now, listen to me. That was dirty, that ain't us. Here's what we do, we're gonna play with our pads, every moment."

The play occurred early in the second quarter when USC linebacker Desman Stephens II hit Moore in the head area while the quarterback was sliding to the ground.

Stephens was assessed a personal foul for targeting and ejected from the game, and Dylan Raiola threw a touchdown pass two plays later after replacing Moore to give the Ducks a 10-7 lead.

Moore was carted off the field, and Lanning later announced that he was diagnosed with a concussion.

With their star quarterback out, the Ducks played an inspired game and went on to secure a 41-27 road win over the then-No. 12 Trojans.

Oregon moved up from No. 20 to No. 15 in the Associated Press Top 25 Poll with the win, while USC dropped to No. 18.

It is unclear how much time Moore will have to miss, but until he is able to return, Raiola figures to be the Ducks' quarterback after throwing for 289 yards and two touchdowns in Saturday's victory.

articles.standfirst: Los amarillos afrontan un mes con dos partidos Champions, la visita al Bernabéu y dos derbis regionales
articles.summary: Los amarillos afrontan un mes con dos partidos Champions, la visita al Bernabéu y dos derbis regionales
articles.body: El Villarreal hará bien en cargar pilas durante este largo parón con vistas al exigente calendario que se le avecina. Y es que mes de octubre se convierte en un prueba de fuego para medir la recuperación que el equipo amarillo experimento justo antes de que la Liga se detuviera por las fechas FIFA. Los de Iñigo Pérez deberán afrontar en poco más de dos semanas varios partidos ante algunos de los equipos más importantes de Europa además de un par de partidos de máxima intensidad como siempre son los derbis de rivalidad regional. El regreso a la competición no puede tener un escenario más imponente cómo será el Santiago Bernabéu el próximo 10 de octubre desde las 21h. Los azulejeros buscarán la sorpresa en un estadio en el que consiguió por última vez la victoria en la temporada 22/23 gracias al doblete de un pletórico Chukwueze. Sin apenas tiempo para el descanso tres días después les espera uno de los partidos más importantes de la temporada con la visita del Nápoles al Estadio de La Cerámica. Todo lo que no sea una victoria ante los italianos, complicaría sobremanera cualquier opción de superar la fase de grupos y hará que revolotee la sombra del fracaso europeo de la pasada temporada. Tras esta explosiva “rentrée” a la competición, el sábado 17 de octubre recibirá la visita del Elche en el primero de los derbis que les esperan en el intervalo de una semana. Un duelo especialmente complicado al estar entre dos complicadísimos partidos europeos. El ya mentado ante el Nápoles y el que el martes 20 de octubre enfrentarán en Anfield ante el Liverpool, uno de los escenarios más dificultosos del continente. La exigente terna se cerrará en Mestalla ante el Valencia, en lo que nunca es un partido más para ambos equipos y que obliga a dar un extra. Ante el cuadro che cerrará un mes futbolístico que, a buen seguro, medirá el grado de recuperación de los amarillos y parte de sus aspiraciones reales en este momento de la temporada.

articles.title: Manchester City respond to Premier League’s seismic ruling of guilt over majority of 115 charges
articles.summary: The club said it was ‘disappointed and surprised’ by the independent commission’s verdict
articles.body:
Manchester City have protested their innocence despite the Premier League 's ruling that the club was guilty of the majority of the 115 charges levied against it for breaches of the league's financial rules.

The club issued a statement in response to the Premier League's seismic judgement , which was published on Tuesday after reports first emerged last Friday that a verdict had been reached.

Sanctions have yet to be decided in the case and City have until Friday 2 October to appeal the independent commission's findings. The commission was appointed after a four-year investigation into the charges, which span a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018, during which time City won eight trophies.

A club statement read: " Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, that has been published today.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

"The Club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

The Premier League statement on the findings read: "An independent Commission has found Manchester City FC guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a 9-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League's investigation.

"The independent Commission found that Manchester City arranged 'sham' commercial deals with a number of its sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees."

articles.title: Eagles news: Sean Mannion's offense looking too much like Kevin Patullo's
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles had a complete meltdown on Monday Night Football. Philadelphia could not move the ball against Chicago, only managing to score seven...
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles had a complete meltdown on Monday Night Football . Philadelphia could not move the ball against Chicago, only managing to score seven points. The problems with Philly's offense look eerily similar to how the team struggled under Kevin Patullo in 2025.

Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion can not be pleased with his unit after Week 3. Philly recorded an EPA/drive of -1.68 against Chicago, the worst performance of the Nick Sirianni era per The Athletic's Zach Berman.

To make matters worse, the Eagles have ranked near the bottom of the league in three-and-outs over the past two seasons. In that respect, there's really no difference between the results that Patullo and Mannion have delivered.

"Just kind of being off schedule there, not being in third-and-long, being in second-and-long, and we have to fix that," Sirianni said. "You can't go backwards."

Fortunately, Philly's biggest stars on offense are taking it upon themselves to fix this problem.

Quarterback Jalen Hurts is taking responsibility for the team's lack of success on third downs. Especially during Monday's brutal loss to the Bears.

"That's a complete team effort that starts with me," Hurts said. "Making sure we're in the right play. Making sure we're managing in a way where we're ahead of the sticks. And situationally, I gotta play better ball. Gotta play better ball. Third down was a very big down for us, and that's been a very big down for us in these first two games. And today we were not good enough, and I wasn't good enough. Fourth down I wasn't good enough, as well."

Now it is much easier said than done to completely fix an NFL offense. But the Eagles are one step ahead of most because they know exactly what is going wrong.

It will be interesting to see what improvements the Eagles make in their next matchup.

articles.title: Manchester City prodigy makes USMNT debut ahead of 2027 Premier League move
articles.summary: Set to join Manchester City in 2027, Cavan Sullivan, now 17, made his U.S. Men's National Team debut in a friendly win over Peru after a standout run for Phi...
articles.body:
In precisely 12 months, Cavan Sullivan will officially become a Manchester City player.

Whether the exceptionally gifted teenager will integrate directly into the first-team environment, settle into the academy structure, or head out on loan remains uncertain. However, this past weekend offered a preview of exactly what City have secured in the midfielder.

Sullivan, who celebrated his 17th birthday on Monday and will complete his move to City when he turns 18, earned his U.S. Men's National Team debut on Saturday, featuring for 60 minutes in the friendly victory over Peru.

Mauricio Pochettino has handed the midfielder his maiden cap following an impressive stretch of performances in Major League Soccer that has seen Sullivan excel for Philadelphia Union despite being just 16 years old. Since the summer FIFA World Cup intermission, no player has registered more goal contributions than the youngster, with only one individual matching Sullivan's tally of 13—a certain Lionel Messi . Elite company for a talent City secured back in 2024, via the Manchester Evening News .

This campaign has seen the teenager deliver a breakout season that his ability has long indicated was inevitable. Coaches at both club and national team level have been cautious not to accelerate his development prematurely, but his performances this year made him virtually impossible for Pochettino to overlook.

"If we only talk about his performance, he's doing really well in his club in Philadelphia. Talking only about that, I think he's ready, but the rest of the players too," Pochettino said of Sullivan ahead of the weekend win over Peru. "He's mature enough on the field."

Sullivan delivered a poised display in what proved to be a straightforward USMNT win, with numerous emerging talents spearheading the American squad as they set their sights on the 2030 World Cup.

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

"It was a really special day for me, my family," said Sullivan "It's crazy that I represented my country [with] the highest level with the Men's National Team, so I'm really happy to have done this. Overall, it was a really amazing night.

"There were nerves [and] I was super excited - a little bit of both," he added. "Pregame was definitely nerve-wracking, yeah."

Pochettino declined to comment specifically on Sullivan following the match, instead offering praise for his entire roster. However, it's evident that the teenager has secured his place in the USMNT setup, which faces Chile on Tuesday before taking on Mexico and Canada .

Sullivan is poised to earn additional caps in the days ahead, and his development this season will have delighted City, who fended off interest from numerous elite clubs worldwide to land his signature. He's been regarded as a future star from an early age due to his obvious ability, but those who've worked closely with Sullivan, who still lives at the family home, emphasize that his skill is matched by his mindset.

"A lot of attention goes on the creative things that he brings to the game," said Union interim head coach Ryan Richter , speaking to ESPN . "But the thing that stands out to me the most is his mentality and his competitiveness and the way that he approaches every single day."

Sullivan would do well to learn from Freddy Adu 's trajectory, another teenage sensation dubbed 'the next Pele' when he inked an MLS deal at 14, the same age Sullivan did two decades afterward. Adu was expected to reach the pinnacle, and though he enjoyed a respectable career, the majority of his professional soccer was played domestically, including a stint at Union.

Adu tweeted his congratulations to Sullivan when the future City star surpassed his MLS record as the youngest debutant at 14 years old in 2024. "That's a hard record to break and the kid did it. Well done and good luck my man," read part of Adu's tweet.

Sullivan's challenge next year will be translating his standout performances in America to European competition and City. However, this is a young player who embraces adversity, perhaps unsurprising given he's the youngest of four brothers. He's self-assured yet humble and courteous, and has handled the considerable spotlight he's been under in recent years admirably.

City maintain regular contact with Sullivan and Union to monitor his development and welfare and the player himself is eager about relocating to Manchester . "Man City, what makes the club is the people," said Sullivan earlier this year. He'll soon be part of the family.

articles.title: Man City found guilty of majority of 115 charges by Premier League
articles.summary: Man City strongly maintain their innocence and claim to have ‘a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence’ to defend themselves, but an independent commissi...
articles.body:
Manchester City have been found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges relating to breaches of the Premier League 's financial rules over a nine-season period.

An independent commission, which was appointed following a four-year investigation to rule over the charges which stretch between 2009 and 2018, ruled that the current Premier League leaders had "sham contracts" arranged for a number of its commercial partners.

The findings also detail how City "relied on sham agreements to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs," while the club reacted to the verdict by underlining they were "disappointed and surprised by the opinion."

And while sanctions are yet to be decided, the verdict, which was widely reported last Friday, has now been confirmed.

A Premier League statement read: "An independent Commission has found Manchester City FC guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over a 9-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League's investigation.

"The independent Commission found that Manchester City arranged 'sham' commercial deals with a number of its sponsors during the period, which were part of a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees."

Manchester City had until Friday, 2 October to appeal, but confirmed in a statement that they will "pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

The Premier League released a 40-page document with details surrounding the case, concerning the hearing dates from 16 September to 31 October 2024, titled: "The Football Association, Premier League Limited and Manchester City Football Club Limited."

City have been accused of not acting in "utmost good faith" while also failing to "provide a true and fair view of the Club's financial position."

While the independent commission also found that "the club made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the Premier League investigation" and "breached duties of co-operation."

articles.standfirst: Asegura que recurrirán ya que el informe "contiene errores materiales evidentes"
articles.summary: Asegura que recurrirán
articles.body: El Manchester City ha emitido un comunicado a los pocos minutos de la resolución de la Premier League en la que se "muestra decepcionado y sorprendido por la opinión de la Comisión de la Premier League". "El club es inocente de las acusaciones formuladas por la Premier League y cuenta con un amplio conjunto de pruebas irrefutables que respaldan todas sus posiciones en relación con este caso. Por lo tanto, el Club actuará con firmeza y, cuando sea necesario, de forma proactiva en todos los foros regulatorios y legales pertinentes". "El proceso de la Premier League sigue en curso, con importantes aspectos aún por concluir. El equipo recurrirá ahora todas las vías legales disponibles, dado que la opinión contiene errores materiales evidentes, tanto de derecho como de principio y de hecho, y resulta injusta". "El Club ha respetado diligentemente el debido proceso durante ocho años, confiando en que la Junta Directiva y el Comité Ejecutivo de la Premier League actuarían como un organismo regulador independiente, imparcial y justo, libre de influencias partidistas". "El Club no puede pronunciarse más al respecto hasta que concluyan todos los procedimientos", cierra el comunicado oficial del equipo. La Premier League confirmó este martes que el Manchester City es culpable de la mayoría de cargos financieros de los que le acusó en febrero de 2023. El club inglés fue acusado hace más de tres años de 115 irregularidades financieras relativas al periodo entre la temporada 2008-2009 y la 2017-2018. Ahora, la comisión independiente determinará cuál es la sanción adecuada para el City, que puede ir desde una multa económica, hasta la pérdida de puntos, descenso de categoría o expulsión de la liga. El City puede apelar hasta el próximo 2 de octubre.
